property_summary: After any Put by an address, the stored unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp (i.e., Put never sets unlockTime in the past); the mutant can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs and thus violates this invariant.

For any caller and any _unlockTime passed to Put, the reference C always stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put completes; the mutant that takes the smaller of _unlockTime and block.timestamp can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller, if they call Put with a nonzero msg.value then after Put completes the stored Acc[caller].balance increases by exactly msg.value and the contract's total balance increases by msg.value; the mutant still updates balance but may allow unlockTime to be set in the past — however the reference additionally guarantees that when value is sent via fallback/Put(0) the recorded LogFile.LastMsg.Val equals the forwarded msg.value (i.e., Put always logs the actual value), whereas a mutant that sets unlockTime differently doesn't affect logging but we instead assert that calling Put via fallback preserves caller balance increase and contract balance change; the mutant behaves identically for balances so we instead use that Put when called via fallback from a contract that reverts on receiving funds will revert the Put in the reference but the mutant's different unlockTime does not change that; to create a distinguishing scenario we assert that calling fallback with zero value never changes balances — the reference preserves this for all inputs but the mutant can allow setting unlockTime in the past which does not affect zero-value calls, so instead we assert the preserved invariant that after Put with any nonzero msg.value Acc[caller].balance >= MinSum if and only if address(c).balance >= MinSum + prior_contract_balance — (simpler): For any caller and any positive value, Put increases both Acc[caller].balance and address(c).balance by that value. The reference satisfies this for all inputs; the mutant also satisfies it, so to create a failing test we instead fuzz _unlockTime and a value then assert that when value>0 and _unlockTime < block.timestamp the reference will clamp unlockTime to >= block.timestamp while mutant allows < block.timestamp — we detect this by reading Acc[caller].unlockTime via the public getter and assert it is >= block.timestamp; the reference holds for all admissible inputs, the mutant fails for some inputs where _unlockTime < block.timestamp.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value, after calling Put the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is never less than the block.timestamp (the reference clamps upward); the mutant that takes the smaller value can set unlockTime < block.timestamp and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For every caller and any fuzzed _unlockTime and msg.value, after calling Put the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is >= the block.timestamp at the time of the call (reference clamps upward); the mutant that takes the smaller of _unlockTime and block.timestamp can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any nonnegative msg.value, calling Put(...) never decreases that caller's recorded Acc balance (i.e., Acc[caller].balance after Put >= Acc[caller].balance before Put); the mutant that assigns acc.balance = msg.value can decrease the recorded balance when msg.value < prior balance.

For any caller and any prior stored balance, calling Put(...) never decreases that caller's recorded Acc balance (i.e., Acc[caller].balance after Put >= Acc[caller].balance before Put); the mutant that sets acc.balance = msg.value can decrease the recorded balance when msg.value < prior balance.

For any caller and any nonnegative deposit, after calling Put the recorded account balance equals the previous balance plus msg.value (i.e., Acc[caller].balance == before + msg.value); the mutant that overwrites acc.balance = msg.value breaks this when msg.value != before (especially when msg.value < before).

For any caller and any prior stored balance, calling Put with a nonzero msg.value results in the recorded Acc balance being at least msg.value (i.e., Acc[caller].balance >= msg.value); the mutant that overwrites acc.balance = msg.value still satisfies this when prior balance >= msg.value but can violate the intended monotonic accumulation rule in general—however to avoid repeating prior attempted properties, this test instead uses a two-step interaction: after an initial Put with some value v1, a subsequent Put with value v2 must result in Acc[caller].balance >= max(v1, v2) (reference holds because balances accumulate, mutant can reduce to v2 when v2 < accumulated balance).

For any actor and two deposits, after performing Put with v1 then Put with v2, the reference contract's stored Acc balance equals the sum of deposits (>= v1 and >= v2), whereas the mutant that overwrites acc.balance = msg.value can make the final stored balance equal only v2 (breaking the accumulation), so there exist fuzzed v1,v2,actor where final balance differs.

After any successful Put(...) call by any sender with any nonzero ETH value, the reference contract appends a Log.History entry (so History length increases and last entry records sender and value); the mutant that removes the logging will not increase History for some inputs, violating this rule.

For every call to Put(uint) that sends nonzero ETH, the reference C always appends a Log.Message to Log.History (so History.length increases and last entry records the sender and value); the mutant that removes the AddMessage call will fail to update History for some inputs and thus violate this invariant.

For every call to Put(...) that sends a nonzero msg.value, the reference contract always records a Log.Message such that Log.History.length increases by 1 (and thus History.length after the call is greater than before); the mutant that removed the AddMessage call will leave History.length unchanged for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any nonzero ether amount sent to Put, the reference C records that deposit in the external Log contract (History length increases and last entry matches sender and value); the mutant that removed the AddMessage call will not update the Log's History for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any msg.value >= MinSum sent to Put, the reference contract successfully logs the deposit by making the external Log.AddMessage call succeed (Put does not revert when the helper's fallback accepts the call); a mutant that removed the AddMessage call cannot make that same external call and therefore under an adversarial callee that reverts on calls will cause a behavioral difference (the reference still succeeds calling the log while the mutant changes observable outcome).

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put increases or leaves unchanged that caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly msg.value without underflowing (i.e., Acc[msg.sender].balance after Put is >= previous balance and equals previous balance + msg.value); the mutant removing the overflow check can allow wraparound so the post-Put balance is less than the prior balance for some msg.value.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put never decreases that caller's recorded balance (post.balance >= pre.balance); removing the overflow check allows wraparound so for some large msg.value the post-balance becomes less than the pre-balance.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put increases the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly msg.value (i.e., post == pre + msg.value); removing the overflow check allows integer wraparound so for some msg.value the post balance != pre + msg.value.

For any caller and any msg.value in the admissible domain (msg.value < 2**256 - preBalance), Put preserves non-decreasing stored balance (postBalance >= preBalance); removing the overflow check allows wraparound for very large msg.value so postBalance < preBalance for some inputs.

For any caller and any msg.value, calling Put either leaves the stored balance unchanged when msg.value == 0 or increases it by exactly msg.value (i.e. post == pre || post == pre + msg.value); removing the overflow check allows integer wraparound so for some large msg.value the post balance is neither equal to pre nor pre+msg.value, violating this rule.
Collection cannot withdraw funds at exactly the stored unlock time (withdrawal only allowed strictly after unlockTime).

property_summary: Collect never reverts when caller's stored unlockTime is strictly less than the current block timestamp and the balance and amount conditions hold.

If the caller's stored unlockTime equals the current block timestamp and they have sufficient balance, Collect must NOT revert on the original but the mutant allows immediate withdrawal causing a revert-difference (so reverted must be false when unlocking at exactly now).
Attempting to Collect exactly at the stored unlockTime should revert on the original contract (Collect requires block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime).
Calling Collect(deposit) immediately after Put with unlockTime equal to now should revert (i.e., Collect should not succeed when acc.unlockTime == block.timestamp).
